content:
# Sirach 29 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 29 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 13

---

## Disagreement 001 — 29:1 "shows-mercy / merciful / lends"
**Verse:** 29:1
**EMET:** "He-who-shows-mercy will-lend to-his-neighbor"
**LOGOS:** "One who shows mercy will lend to his neighbor"
**PNEUMA:** "The merciful person lends to their neighbor"
**Issue:** χρηματίζων — "lending/doing business." The subject is the one who lends (χρηματίζων). The "mercy" element comes earlier in the sentence. PNEUMA's restructuring changes the syntax. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "One who shows mercy lends to his neighbor."

---

## Disagreement 002 — 29:5 "kisses-the-hands / kisses his neighbor's hands"
**Verse:** 29:5
**EMET:** "he-kisses-the-hands of-his-neighbor"
**LOGOS:** "he kisses his neighbor's hands"
**PNEUMA:** "he's kissing his neighbor's hands"
**Issue:** χεῖρας αὐτοῦ καταφιλήσει — "he will kiss his hands." All agree; minor tense difference (PNEUMA uses present continuous). SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "he kisses his neighbor's hands."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 29:6 "count-it-as-a-windfall / count it as a windfall"
**Verse:** 29:6
**EMET:** "he-will-count-it-as-a-windfall"
**LOGOS:** "count it as a windfall"
**PNEUMA:** "acts like he's done you a favor"
**Issue:** εὕρεμα εὑρήσει αὐτό — "he will treat it as found [goods]." EMET and LOGOS's "windfall" is accurate. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the specific "found/windfall" image. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "count it as a windfall."

---

## Disagreement 004 — 29:7 "not from-wickedness / not out of meanness"
**Verse:** 29:7
**EMET:** "not from-wickedness"
**LOGOS:** "not from wickedness"
**PNEUMA:** "not out of meanness"
**Issue:** οὐ κακίᾳ — "not from wickedness/malice." "Meanness" (PNEUMA) is not as theologically precise as "wickedness." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "not from wickedness."

---

## Disagreement 005 — 29:8 "toward-the-lowly / with one who is in humble circumstances"
**Verse:** 29:8
**EMET:** "toward-the-lowly be-long-suffering"
**LOGOS:** "be patient with one who is in humble circumstances"
**PNEUMA:** "be patient with someone who's struggling"
**Issue:** ταπεινῷ — "to the humble/lowly." The term has both economic and spiritual connotation. LOGOS adds "in humble circumstances" (contextually accurate). EMET preserves "lowly" which carries the spiritual dimension. SOPHIA uses "humble circumstances."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "be patient with one who is in humble circumstances."

---

## Disagreement 006 — 29:10 "rust" metaphor
**Verse:** 29:10
**EMET:** "do-not-let-it-rust under a-stone for-loss"
**LOGOS:** "do not let it rust away under a stone and be lost"
**PNEUMA:** "don't let it rust away buried under a stone"
**Issue:** μὴ κατιωθήτω ὑπὸ ἰόν — "do not let it be made rusty/corroded." The image of money buried under a stone and rusting is vivid. All agents preserve the image. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "do not let it rust away under a stone and be lost."

---

## Disagreement 007 — 29:11 "more-than gold / better than gold"
**Verse:** 29:11
**EMET:** "it-will-profit you more-than gold"
**LOGOS:** "it will profit you more than gold"
**PNEUMA:** "it will pay you back better than gold"
**Issue:** ἀντὶ χρυσίου — "in place of gold / instead of gold." PNEUMA's "pay you back" adds a repayment metaphor. EMET/LOGOS are closer. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "it will profit you more than gold."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 29:12 "lock-up almsgiving / store up generosity"
**Verse:** 29:12
**EMET:** "Lock-up almsgiving in your-storerooms"
**LOGOS:** "Lock away almsgiving in your storerooms"
**PNEUMA:** "Store up generosity in your account"
**Issue:** ἀποθήκευσον ἐλεημοσύνην — "store away almsgiving." PNEUMA's "generosity" for ἐλεημοσύνη ("almsgiving") loses the specific practice. "Almsgiving" is the technical term. "In your account" is PNEUMA's banking metaphor (interpretive).
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Lock away almsgiving in your storerooms."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 29:18 "shaken as a sea-wave / like a storm wave"
**Verse:** 29:18
**EMET:** "has-shaken-them as a-sea-wave"
**LOGOS:** "shaken them like a wave of the sea"
**PNEUMA:** "rocked them like a storm wave"
**Issue:** ὡς κῦμα θαλάσσης — "like a wave of the sea." "Storm wave" (PNEUMA) adds "storm" which is not in the Greek. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "shaken them like a wave of the sea."

---

## Disagreement 010 — 29:21 "essentials / necessities" of life
**Verse:** 29:21
**EMET:** "The-essentials of-life are water and bread and clothing and a-house"
**LOGOS:** "The necessities of life are water and bread, clothing and a house"
**PNEUMA:** "The basics of life: water, bread, clothing, and a roof over your head"
**Issue:** ἀρχὴ ζωῆς — "the beginning/foundation of life." "Necessities" (LOGOS) and "essentials" (EMET) both work. PNEUMA's "a roof over your head" for "a house to cover nakedness" loses the specific modesty/nakedness term. SOPHIA preserves the original.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The necessities of life are water and bread, clothing and a house to cover one's nakedness."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 29:22 "roof of logs / shelter of logs / rough shelter"
**Verse:** 29:22
**EMET:** "under a-roof of-logs"
**LOGOS:** "under a shelter of logs"
**PNEUMA:** "under a rough shelter"
**Issue:** ὑπὸ δοκόν — "under a beam/rafter." This is humble dwelling imagery. "Logs" (EMET/LOGOS) is specific to the building material. PNEUMA's "rough shelter" loses the specific image. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "under a shelter of logs."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 29:26-27 quoted speech rendering
**Verses:** 29:26-27
**EMET/LOGOS:** More literal rendering of the quotes
**PNEUMA:** More colloquial ("Clear off, stranger — make way for someone important")
**Issue:** The two quoted speeches are dramatic and realistic. PNEUMA's "Clear off" for "Go away" captures the rudeness but may overstep. The Greek ἄπελθε — "go away/depart" is direct but not as rude as "clear off." SOPHIA uses "Get away" as a middle ground.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Get away, stranger, before the face of an honored guest."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 29:28 "good-nature / good-natured man / generous person"
**Verse:** 29:28
**EMET:** "a-man of-good-nature"
**LOGOS:** "a good-natured man"
**PNEUMA:** "a generous person"
**Issue:** ἀνθρώπου ἐντρεπτικοῦ — "a man of good character/one who is respectful/sensitive." "Generous" (PNEUMA) is interpretive. "Good-natured" is the better rendering. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a good-natured man."
